answer.summary: Grant Lee says Gamma gathered early feedback by putting rough prototypes in front of prospective users and observing them try the product; it also used a dedicated Slack group for repeat users to review early feature ideas.

sections.heading: Test with prospective users
sections.content: Gamma recruited people who regularly made slide decks and had no stake in whether the product succeeded. They were given little context, asked to try Gamma as an alternative to PowerPoint, and prompted to describe what they were thinking and trying to do as they worked through onboarding and tasks. Watching where they struggled helped the team identify what needed fixing.

sections.heading: Use a power-user feedback group
sections.content: For later-stage feature ideas, Gamma created the Gammaster Program: a separate Slack workspace where repeat users saw very early wireframes or functional prototypes and gave initial feedback. For example, the team used this group to test sharing functionality; users could indicate whether the idea was on track, and the team could observe their difficulties.
